## Packages

```{r libraries}
library(rentrez)
library(seqinr)
library(Biostrings)
```

---

## 1. Obtain sequences from NCBI and save to a single FASTA file

We use `rentrez` to search and fetch the complete genome sequences of the 5 viruses from NCBI Nucleotide.

```{r fetch-sequences}
# Accession numbers for complete genomes
accessions <- c(
  Zika          = "NC_012532",   # Zika virus, complete genome
  SARS          = "NC_004718",   # SARS coronavirus, complete genome
  COVID19       = "NC_045512",   # Wuhan-Hu-1 (SARS-CoV-2), complete genome
  MERS          = "NC_019843",   # MERS coronavirus, complete genome
  Dengue1       = "NC_001477"    # Dengue virus 1, complete genome
)

# Fetch sequences in FASTA format
seqs_fasta <- entrez_fetch(
  db       = "nucleotide",
  id       = accessions,
  rettype  = "fasta",
  retmode  = "text"
)

# Save all 5 sequences into a single FASTA file
writeLines(seqs_fasta, "virus_sequences.fasta")
cat("FASTA file saved: virus_sequences.fasta\n")
```

---

## 2. Size of each sequence

```{r sequence-size}
# Read the FASTA file with seqinr
seqs <- read.fasta("virus_sequences.fasta", seqtype = "DNA", as.string = FALSE)

# Rename for clarity
names(seqs) <- c("Zika", "SARS-CoV-1", "SARS-CoV-2 (Wuhan-Hu-1)", "MERS-CoV", "Dengue 1")

# Get lengths
sizes <- sapply(seqs, length)
size_df <- data.frame(
  Virus  = names(sizes),
  Length = sizes,
  row.names = NULL
)

knitr::kable(size_df, caption = "Sequence length (nucleotides) of each virus")
```

---

## 3. Nucleotide composition of each sequence

```{r nucleotide-composition}
# Compute base frequencies
comp_list <- lapply(seqs, table)
comp_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(comp_list), function(v) {
  tb <- comp_list[[v]]
  bases <- c("a", "c", "g", "t")
  counts <- setNames(as.integer(tb[bases]), toupper(bases))
  counts[is.na(counts)] <- 0
  data.frame(Virus = v, t(counts))
}))

knitr::kable(comp_df, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Nucleotide composition (raw counts) of each virus")
```

---

## 4. GC content of each virus

```{r gc-content}
gc_values <- sapply(seqs, function(s) {
  tb <- table(s)
  g  <- ifelse("g" %in% names(tb), tb["g"], 0)
  c_ <- ifelse("c" %in% names(tb), tb["c"], 0)
  round((g + c_) / length(s) * 100, 2)
})

gc_df <- data.frame(
  Virus      = names(gc_values),
  GC_content = paste0(gc_values, "%"),
  row.names  = NULL
)

knitr::kable(gc_df, caption = "GC content (%) of each virus")
```

---

## 5. Summary plot — nucleotide composition comparison

```{r composition-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# Reshape to long format
comp_long <- comp_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("A", "C", "G", "T"),
               names_to  = "Nucleotide",
               values_to = "Count") %>%
  group_by(Virus) %>%
  mutate(Proportion = Count / sum(Count) * 100)

ggplot(comp_long, aes(x = Virus, y = Proportion, fill = Nucleotide)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(A = "#4CAF50", C = "#2196F3",
                               G = "#FF9800", T = "#F44336")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Nucleotide Composition Comparison",
    subtitle = "5 complete virus genomes",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Proportion (%)",
    fill     = "Nucleotide"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position  = "right"
  )
```

## H1N1 Influenza — Mexico 2009 (8 segments)

Using the NCBI Influenza Virus Database, we retrieve all 8 genomic segments of the H1N1 strain that appeared in Mexico in 2009.

```{r h1n1-segments}
# Accession numbers for the 8 segments of A/Mexico/2009 H1N1
# Source: NCBI Influenza Virus Database
h1n1_acc <- c(
  PB2 = "GQ117044",   # Segment 1 - PB2
  PB1 = "GQ117045",   # Segment 2 - PB1
  PA  = "GQ117046",   # Segment 3 - PA
  HA  = "GQ117047",   # Segment 4 - HA (hemagglutinin)
  NP  = "GQ117048",   # Segment 5 - NP
  NA_ = "GQ117049",   # Segment 6 - NA (neuraminidase)
  M   = "GQ117050",   # Segment 7 - M (M1/M2)
  NS  = "GQ117051"    # Segment 8 - NS (NS1/NEP)
)

# Fetch all 8 segments
h1n1_fasta <- entrez_fetch(
  db      = "nucleotide",
  id      = h1n1_acc,
  rettype = "fasta",
  retmode = "text"
)

writeLines(h1n1_fasta, "h1n1_mexico_2009_segments.fasta")
cat("H1N1 FASTA file saved: h1n1_mexico_2009_segments.fasta\n")

# Read and show segment sizes
h1n1_seqs <- read.fasta("h1n1_mexico_2009_segments.fasta",
                         seqtype = "DNA", as.string = FALSE)
names(h1n1_seqs) <- names(h1n1_acc)

h1n1_sizes <- sapply(h1n1_seqs, length)
h1n1_df <- data.frame(
  Segment   = names(h1n1_sizes),
  Accession = h1n1_acc,
  Length    = h1n1_sizes,
  row.names = NULL
)

knitr::kable(h1n1_df, caption = "H1N1 Mexico 2009 — 8 genomic segments")
```
